questions.q: Why is curiosity called the heart of science?
questions.a: Asking 'why' about everyday happenings leads to questions, experiments and discoveries.

questions.q: Give one example of a discovery that began with a simple question.
questions.a: Newton asking why apples fall led to the law of gravitation.

questions.q: What attitude makes a good scientist?
questions.a: Curiosity, honesty in recording results, patience and willingness to be proved wrong.

concepts.title: Working Like a Scientist: Methods and Safety

questions.q: List the steps of the scientific method in order.
questions.a: Observe, ask a question, form a hypothesis, test by experiment, analyse results and conclude.

questions.q: Why is a control set-up used in experiments?
questions.a: It stays unchanged so the effect of the one changed factor can be seen clearly.

questions.q: Name two safety rules for a laboratory.
questions.a: Wear safety gear (goggles, apron) and never taste or directly smell chemicals.

concepts.title: Science in Society and Everyday Life

questions.q: How does science help in daily life? Give two examples.
questions.a: Vaccines and antibiotics protect health; electricity and machines ease work and transport.

questions.q: Name a scientific advance that changed farming.
questions.a: High-yielding seeds, fertilisers and irrigation of the Green Revolution raised food production.
Weapons and pollution show that science must be guided by ethics and law.
